clue.text: Circles rook with pieces following opponent's opening

indicators.note: following tells us the pieces before it come after the other letter in the answer
an opening is the start of something, so only the first letter of the word before it is kept

parts.note: the first letter of opponent's
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
pieces are bits

explanation.surface: A chess move: the rook and other pieces swing round after the opponent opens the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits as a verb means goes round in a loop, the same as circles does.

clue.text: Painting, superficially attractive, depicting ecological problem at sea

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
slick means glossy but shallow

explanation.surface: A slick, glossy painting showing an environmental disaster at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil slick is a film of spilled oil spreading on the sea, damaging wildlife.

clue.text: Rodgers and Hart song, sad, second on

parts.note: to feel blue is to feel sad
a mo is a moment, a second
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad Rodgers and Hart number, coming on second in the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Moon is a 1934 popular song by the songwriting team of Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart.

clue.text: Greek character volunteers after article

indicators.note: after tells us the order: the volunteers come behind the article

parts.note: the definite article
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek person enlisting with a volunteer force after reading an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, written like an O with a bar.

clue.text: Catch post in western extremity

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Someone catching the post at the far west end of a route.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost tip of mainland England, in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Land's End is the far south-western point of England, its extreme western headland.

clue.text: Type of cattle under an age BSE affected?

indicators.note: affected means changed by an illness, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a breed of cattle below a certain age is hit by mad cow disease.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease, which hit British cattle in the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen Angus is a hornless black beef breed originating in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Unfortunately did for two found washed up on a beach?

definitions.text: found washed up on a beach?
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase; read it as 'something found washed up on a beach'

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Sadly, something did for two people, who were later found washed up on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftwood is timber carried by the sea and left on the shore, the classic beachcombing find.

clue.text: Carry on with former nurse

parts.note: ex means former
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Continuing to work alongside a nurse who used to be on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to make it continue further, so carry on is a synonym.

clue.text: Poet in study, in need of a drink first

indicators.note: first places the thirsty description at the front, ahead of the room

parts.note: dry means thirsty
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A poet at work in the study, wanting a drink before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dryden was the leading English poet of the late 17th century.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden, England's first Poet Laureate, wrote satirical and dramatic verse.

clue.text: 25 left by river

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Something abandoned at the side of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25-across, PARASITE, which is the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small insect parasite living on the skin or hair of its host.

clue.text: What may be taught at school about helium, head of mathematics is to test

definitions.text: What may be taught at school

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
He is the chemical symbol for helium

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of mathematics
taken as written
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A school lesson about helium, where the head of maths is set to run a test.
explanation.walkthrough: The helium and test make the surface feel like a science class, which is apt for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry is a science subject on the school timetable, so it is something that may be taught.

clue.text: Sort to leave acting role

parts.note: an odd sort is an odd character
to part is to leave

explanation.surface: Instructions to sort out who must leave an acting role.
explanation.definitionFit: A character part is a stage or screen role portraying an eccentric or distinctive person.

clue.text: Letter from Greece about a dance

indicators.note: about means going round, so the Greek letter wraps around what follows

parts.note: lambda is the Greek letter L
taken as written

explanation.surface: A letter arriving from Greece concerning a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance popular in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Spanish wine imbibed by river results in easing of tension

indicators.note: something imbibed is swallowed and held inside the drinker

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Sharing a bottle of Spanish wine by the river makes everyone relax.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent, a dark red wine from Spain, is mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Detente is the diplomatic term for a relaxation of strained relations between countries.

clue.text: Pretty sweet carton

definitions.meaning: first meaning: conventionally pretty, like the picture on a box lid
second meaning: a box that holds chocolates

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests a rather sweet carton; split, the adjective and the literal container are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate-box describes a picturesque, sentimental prettiness, and literally it is a container for confectionery.

clue.text: Sold us roe, processed, having no smell

indicators.note: processed food has been worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A fishmonger sold us processed fish eggs with no smell at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Odourless means without any scent, exactly lacking a smell.

clue.text: Cushy job at home in stable

indicators.note: in places the first part inside the word that follows

parts.note: stable means secure
at home is in

explanation.surface: A cushy job working from home in a horse stable.
explanation.walkthrough: Stable looks like a noun for horses but is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post that pays but requires little or no work.

clue.text: Ringing dope in factory

indicators.note: in places the first part inside the word that follows

parts.note: a plant is a factory
dope and gen both mean information

explanation.surface: A drug-filled factory where the phones keep ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope here is slang for inside information, not drugs; gen is the British slang equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant, often mournful sound, such as a bell's ringing.

clue.text: Dorset lighthouse seen in harbour — come ashore on account

parts.note: a port is a harbour
to land is to come ashore
a bill is an account of what is owed

explanation.surface: A lighthouse spotted from a harbour by someone landing who has a tab to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Portland Bill is the southern tip of the Isle of Portland in Dorset, on England's south coast, known for its red-and-white lighthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Portland Bill is a headland in Dorset whose name is commonly used for its famous lighthouse.

clue.text: Step one is to climb across cold mass covering the top of Everest?

definitions.text: mass covering the top of Everest?

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards
across means spanning something, so it goes around the letter for cold

parts.note: a pace is a step
I is the Roman numeral one
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Mountaineering advice: the first step is to cross the cold to reach Everest's summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that Everest's summit is not strictly a polar ice cap.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent dome of ice covering high ground, apt for a peak's frozen top.

clue.text: Don't forget about leaving part

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so those letters drop out of the longer word

parts.note: don't forget means remember
re means about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A reminder not to forget someone who is leaving and parting company.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is a limb or a constituent piece of a whole, so a part.

clue.text: Le Carré novel, more readable

indicators.note: novel means new, so the name is made into something new by rearranging

parts.note: the spy novelist's surname, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A John le Carré spy novel that is easier to read than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book by the author, but it is the signal to rearrange his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearer means easier to understand, which is what more readable prose is.

clue.text: Vessel's gone out with everybody on board

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
on board means inside a ship, so this goes within the other letters

parts.note: the word gone rearranged
everybody is all

explanation.surface: A ship has left harbour with all its passengers aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship of the 15th to 17th centuries, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Circles vowel in error

parts.note: laps are circuits of a track
E is one of the vowels

explanation.surface: Someone circles a vowel on a page, marking a spelling mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor mistake, a momentary failure of concentration.

clue.text: Cabins for the upwardly mobile?

parts.note: surface reading: homes for social climbers, people rising in status; setter's reading: cabins that literally travel uphill, hauled along a wire

explanation.walkthrough: Upwardly mobile usually means ambitious people moving up in society; here it means literally carried up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cabins suspended from a moving wire rope that carry passengers up slopes.

clue.text: Quiet old character in trim

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a rune is a letter of an ancient alphabet

explanation.surface: A quiet old eccentric who keeps in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune a plant or a text is to cut it back, which is what trimming does.

clue.text: Hanger-on ruined pair's tea

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: An unwelcome guest has spoiled a couple's afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite, figuratively, is a person who lives off others, a sponger or hanger-on.

clue.text: Want to change sides

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lack or shortcoming
second meaning: to desert one's country or party for the other

explanation.walkthrough: Want reads as a verb of desire, but it is the old noun sense of lack.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a flaw or deficiency; as a verb it means to abandon allegiance for a rival.
